On ngesk2/crx-runtime: I pulled the repo through the GitHub connector and the biggest lesson is actually very aligned with what you're building now. This repository is not a finished runtime to import wholesale. It is a constitutional/forensic corpus with a thin runtime, a lot of authority doctrine, explicit anti-duplication rules, and strong ideas about replay, permissions, event lineage, and agent non-sovereignty. Its own root directive says it is not an AI app or an automation playground; it defines itself as a deterministic constitutional substrate and explicitly says agents are execution transforms, not authorities. It also requires reuse-before-create, one canonical event model, worktrees, bounded agent permissions, replay, policy, and audit lineage. That makes it useful as a harvest source for primitives and discipline, not as a replacement architecture for PING. I would send the 24-hour fleet this: GO GO GO — 24-HOUR CONVERGENCE SPRINT. USE EVERY AVAILABLE AGENT, BUT DO NOT TURN THIS INTO AGENT CHAOS. The most valuable things to harvest from CRX are not its folder tree or “constitutional” vocabulary. They are: explicit worker permissions, worktree isolation, replayable change evidence, anti-shadow-system discipline, proposal/execution separation, and the doctrine that agents are transforms rather than truth owners.
